gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the two-box Renogy setup (REGO 12V 3000W inverter charger at $989.99 plus a Rover Lite 60A MPPT controller at $249.99, $1,239.98 in total) costs $58.02 less than ChatGPT's 'top pick', the ACOPOWER 3000W/12V all-in-one at $1,298. It also doesn't state that moving to 24V brings 3000W all-in-one units with built-in MPPT down to $401 (Sun Gold Power) or $330 for 4000W (PowMr).
standout_why: Every result ChatGPT got is a renogy.com page: the REGO 12V 3000W inverter charger (three URLs), the 2000W/3000W 12V HF inverter charger, the 3000W 12V inverter, solar kits, the RV Solution and a split-phase blog post. Those pages price Renogy items one by one. None prices a 12V all-in-one with built-in MPPT, because Renogy's own store search returned none (its only solar inverter chargers are 48V). None adds up REGO plus an MPPT controller against an all-in-one, and none gives 24V all-in-one prices. ChatGPT's answer says 24V/48V is 'more practical' above about 2,000W but gives no price for that route. It also names EG4 as a top 12V brand even though EG4's inverter page lists no model marked 12V.
decides: This shifts the pick. For a shopper set on 12V, the only 12V/120V all-in-one with MPPT confirmed on a US maker store is the ACOPOWER at $1,298, and it costs more than Renogy's REGO plus Rover Lite at $1,239.98. So 'all-in-one' buys fewer boxes, not a lower price. A shopper who can move to a 24V battery gets a 3000W all-in-one with 80A/60A MPPT for $401 (Sun Gold Power, one of our affiliate programs), about $897 less than the ACOPOWER. A 24V LiFePO4 battery is available on our catalog (Redodo 24V 100Ah). EG4 drops out for 12V.
